newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA political wing gets permit for demonstration.
newsitem.headline: ETA political wing gets permit for demonstration.

text.p: The government of Spain's Basque region gave permission on Thursday for the guerrilla group ETA's political wing to stage a demonstration on Sunday despite concerns it could turn violent.

A march planned for last Saturday by Herri Batasuna, a radical separatist party allied with ETA, was banned to avert a backlash from people angered by the rebels' killing of a young Basque town councillor earlier this month.
"The Basque government Interior Department...has decided to authorise the demonstration called by Herri Batasuna for next Sunday in San Sebastian," the statement said.

Basque officials said there would be heavy security on hand due to lingering tensions over ETA's kidnapping and killing of 29-year-old politician Miguel Angel Blanco. Herri Batasuna's past demonstrations have been flashpoints of violence.

Authorities are concerned about possible civilian clashes following huge demonstrations across Spain last week in which an estimated six million people demanded an end to ETA violence. Most of the marches were peaceful although there were sporadic attacks on Herri Batasuna members and offices.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed more than 800 people in nearly 30 years of fighting for an independent Basque state.
